Material drift in the Inven page: despite the STRICTLY EXCLUDE language, a large share of returned rows are telecom/fiber-only contractors, gas/oil pipeline contractors, wet-utility (water/sewer) excavators, civil/foundation firms, engineering-design-only firms, and a few fabricators/manufacturers (e.g. Klute, M.D. Henry, Western Utility Telecom) - the triage script only gates a subset of these, so the T3 survivor list needs a manual on-thesis pass before outreach.

notes: Inven build had no missing_criterion or clarification_needed; only interpretation note: US private-company reported financials unavailable, so the $5-50M revenue filter runs on estimated latest-year revenue (estimates included). No refinement needed. Ownership mapped to private_unknown/family_owned/angel/family_office, which matches the not-PE-backed/not-subsidiary reading.
Inven total_results 24,414 (retrievable 10,000); pulled top 200 rows in a single run as instructed. credits_used: screening 1, export 200.

Grata: 2 calls total (6 tokens), page 1 only for both variants. Page 2 was NOT fetched for either set: variant 1 page 1 was dominated by residential/commercial general electrical contractors (drift from 'industrial electrical troubleshooting'), and variant 2 page 1 by distributors, panel shops, HVAC/irrigation dealers and equipment manufacturers (drift from 'VFD repair'). Totals: variant 1 = 39, variant 2 = 34; 25 rows captured per variant.

Grata's year_founded_max=2016 was translated to company_age [10,61], which also excludes pre-1965 founding years; a few very old firms may have been silently cut from Grata results (Inven had no such cap).

Triage script (sole dedupe/triage authority) dropped 81 known rows (master/DQ/Nurture/screened/outreach/wave-1, incl. cross-source dupes such as Grata's Cates Control Systems, B.L. Smith, Scott Testing, C+D Electric Motors, Lewis Electric Motor Repair, Caldwell, Global Power dupes) and 0 no-domain rows; 169 survivors returned exactly as written (desc capped at 400 chars). Survivor priorities: 122 P2-candidate, 38 DQ-candidate (gate reasons in note field, mostly residential/home-services/solar/HVAC language), 9 P3-candidate (below $5M revenue box).

Watchouts in survivors: Metrowest Group carries a .com.au domain and appears Australia-operating despite the US filter (likely geography drift); script AGE FLAGs on Feed Yard Industrial Solutions (2019) and Industrial Maintenance Solutions (2017); several Grata survivors (KR Automation, Hope Electric, Moley Magnetics, North Central Irrigation, Hardy Pro-Air) read as distributor/panel-shop/equipment-led despite P2 tags - worth a human look against the service-led thesis.
No failed or retried calls; both sources returned successfully.
verify_notes: Systematic triage inflation found: roughly 30 P2-candidates carried the boilerplate note 'service/maintenance/testing language' when the description actually shows only construction/installation/design-build language. All such rows were downgraded to P3-candidate; P2 was retained only where maintenance, repair, troubleshooting, testing/calibration, commissioning, emergency service, or 24/7 support is explicit in the description.

Residential DQs left untouched per the client's literal residential gate (Bills Electric, Grotberg, Northside, Emory, Biskamp, Sollmann, Red River, Keithly, GTG, Steve's, McNeer, Rossmann, Travis, D&H, Positive, Momentum, Alpine, Triple Crown, Sierra Valley, Allied Industrial, Precision Electric Co, Brandenburg, Everingham, Ellis, Mirarchi). Solar gates (Goldhorn, Halligan, ResCom) and off-trade HVAC gates (Kotz, GTG, Corporate Air, Interactive Building, Roessler, Electro Power) are fair on the quoted text and stand. Power And Control's distributor gate stands (self-described wholesale distributor).

Two DQ misfires corrected with REVIEW: primeelectrical.net (structured cabling is a secondary line, not a stated exclusion) and graphicelectric.org (gate confused serving manufacturers with being one). smartelectriccompanyinc.com corrected DQ->P3 with REVIEW (incidental HVAC line on an electrical-led firm, but installation-led).

Two new DQs: ese-co.com (self-described electrical supply company - distributor) and krautomationinc.com (surplus parts resale is primary). metrowest.com.au DQ'd as an Australian business misfiled under a Washington HQ.

Data-quality flags on rows kept as P2: aecinc.us description claims ~180 electricians vs emp=34 and rev $33.4M - if 180 electricians is right, revenue likely exceeds the $50M box; elliselectricnwi... n/a; eliteelectrical.net shows 83 emp vs $7.6M rev; cates.com shows 88 emp vs $10.3M rev. Recommend revenue re-verification before outreach.

brandonclark.com kept P2 but is really a motor/transformer repair and rewind shop (as are electricmotorshop.com, vaughnelectric.com, texasoilelectric.com, aandwelectric.com); if a separate motor-repair bucket exists among T1-T6/S7-S10 they may belong there - no moves recorded because other bucket definitions were not provided.
Age flags preserved as-is: fyi.solutions (2019) and imsnation.com (2017) remain P2-candidates with their existing under-10-years flags.

Watermark, Intermountain, El-Hy-Mec, Tucker, Automation Control Co, Electronic Maintenance Associates, Precision Electronics, First Electric Motor, and D Electric Motors correctly sit at P3 on sub-$5M revenue; no changes.

notes: Inven build flagged missing_criterion 'light-industrial facilities'; refined once (search_id 407f071ad20c4a41ab0c2cdbded9c445) to add it; final estimate 6510 results. Clarification on 'not PE-backed' resolved from thesis without asking: excluded all PE-backed; ownership types applied were private_unknown, family_owned, venture_capital, angel, family_office (VC/angel included as non-PE private).
Inven interpretation note: US private reported financials unavailable, so the $5-50M revenue filter uses estimated latest-year revenue only.

MATERIAL DRIFT in Inven results: a large share of the 200 exported rows are electrical/industrial DISTRIBUTORS, MRO suppliers, motor/servo repair shops, and even aviation/lubricants suppliers rather than commercial electrical contractors with recurring service departments - the semantic match drifted toward 'maintenance supply/repair' language. Triage gated many (94 of 210 survivors are DQ-candidates, mostly distribution/resale, manufacturer, residential, off-trade gates), but a number of distributors/motor shops passed as P2 on generic service/maintenance language - recommend a skeptical screen of Inven P2s for this bucket. Survivor priority mix: 96 P2-candidate, 20 P3-candidate, 94 DQ-candidate.

Some Inven rows have non-US operations despite the US HQ filter: Dahlrail (Norway/Sweden/Netherlands rail), NEO-CAM (Cameroon), Access Electrical (.co.uk); also several rows look like motor-repair (S7 bucket) rather than T5 - left in per triage-authority rule.

Grata: variant 1 (electrical preventive maintenance program / facility electrical services) = 258 total; variant 2 (emergency electrical service commercial / electrical service department) = 162 total; page 1 only for both (page 2 skipped: both pages mixed construction-led, residential-mixed and fire-alarm/security contractors, not mostly on-thesis). 2 Grata calls total, under the 5-call cap.

Triage: in=250 (200 Inven + 50 Grata), survivors=210, dropped_known=40, nodemain=0. No calls failed; no retries needed. Candidates returned exactly as triage script wrote them with desc capped at 400 chars.
verify_notes: Off-thesis rationale: su-group.com is a vendor-neutral maintenance-contract consolidation/administration business (chooses other providers, delivers nothing itself); reliamag.com is a reliability consulting/training/content firm (2024 vintage); tricorindustrialinc.com sells janitorial/sanitation supplies; dahlrail.com is European (Norway/Sweden/Netherlands) rolling-stock maintenance and spares; dsctrading.com is an aviation parts supplier; ttnfleetsolutions.com is vehicle fleet maintenance. None are US electrical infrastructure services.

Wave-2 P2 pool was heavily contaminated with supply houses and MRO distributors carrying the boilerplate triage note 'service/maintenance/testing language' with no such language in the description — 25+ P2s corrected to DQ on the distribution gate alone. The triage note text appears to have been applied indiscriminately.

P2s that survived challenge (kept as-is): gohispeed.com, electricmotorshop.com, burfordinc.com, vaughnelectric.com, knightelectrical.com, pylmanpower.com, scottarm.com, coreelectric.net, ridgeview-mc.com, bandhelectric.com, alaelectric.com, cascade-machinery.com, omirepair.com, flolo.com, semw.net, industrialelectricalco.com, magnaproducts.com, universalservo.com, msenergy.com, iemco.com, southernwinding.com, matlockelectric.com, uigcorp.com, ivsincorporated.com, americanindustrialinc.com, skileselectric.com, allenselectricmotors.com, emsindustrial.com, lcelectricinc.com, qdelectrical.com, swetexas.com, maderelectricmotors.com, ridgelineei.com, eecmotor.com, aandwelectric.com, gesrepair.com, blsmithelectric.com, vesdfw.com, controlrepair.com, 360energysolutions.net, bestwayelectric.com, litcoautomation.com, bolt-electric.com, twinelectricltd.com, jwelectric.com, ajgoulderelectric.com, viaelectric.com — all show genuine repair/maintenance delivery, in-box revenue, no gate language, no sponsor.

Data conflicts flagged (kept at current priority, verify before outreach): twinelectricltd.com HQ listed Show Low AZ but description says Chicago; jwelectric.com HQ Hammond IN but description says Utah since 1980; lcelectricinc.com HQ Mount Carmel PA but description says Central Florida.

ceddallas.com and cedindustrialtx.com carry the CED brand (Consolidated Electrical Distributors, a large national) — DQ stands on distribution, and these are almost certainly branches/subsidiaries, a second independent gate.

Revenue-box breaches inside already-DQ'd rows: alexander-electric.com ($73.4M), cdaviselectric.com ($69.7M), emoryelectric.com ($51.3M) — above box, DQ stands regardless. lakecable.com shows 250 employees against a $30M estimate; likely well above box (DQ on manufacturer anyway).

Left as-is but weak: saftgard.com (P3) is a PPE products business with no service line — DQ on manual review would be defensible; a-c-s.com (P3) is a power-cord product company, likely maker/reseller; access-electrical.co.uk (DQ) shows a UK domain and 'Ltd' despite a Georgia HQ — geography suspect.

Fire-alarm gates on beckstromelectric.com and hannonelectricinc.com applied literally per client's gate even though both are otherwise strong commercial electrical service firms with fire alarm as one line — worth client confirmation that the gate is any-mention rather than lead-line.

premcoinc.net kept DQ: HVAC appears within its own repair trade ('electric motors, pumps, and HVAC systems'), unlike dreisilker.com where HVAC was only a customer industry — that distinction drove the one un-DQ.
core4technologies.com: the 'manufacturer (self)' gate quote is a misread (it is a manufacturers' REP, not a manufacturer), but the distribution/rep gate independently holds — DQ unchanged.

industrialelectricalco.com (165 emp / $28M) and 360energysolutions.net ('over 65 years' vs 2013 founding) have internal inconsistencies but plausible service-business profiles — kept P2 with this flag.

notes: Inven build had no missing_criterion and no clarification_needed, so no refinement pass was used. Interpretation notes worth keeping: (1) reported financials are unavailable for US private companies, so the $5-50M revenue filter ran on estimated latest-year revenue only (all rev values are estimates, hence the long decimals); (2) Inven's 'private' ownership category is a catch-all that may still contain unlabeled subsidiaries.

Inven total_results 14,269 (retrievable 10,000) is far larger than the 200 rows exported - the descriptive-prompt match is broad. The top-200 ranked rows were mostly on-thesis critical-power/UPS/generator service firms, but generic commercial electrical contractors appear deeper in the ranking; a deeper wave could page further with offset if T6 needs more volume.

Grata variant 1 (generator preventive maintenance / emergency power system testing, 231 results) drifted heavily off-thesis: page 1 was dominated by auto repair and tire shops, flood restoration, and residential trades - Grata's core-focus semantic expansion latched onto 'preventive maintenance' generically. Page 2 was NOT fetched for this set per the mostly-on-thesis rule; its off-thesis rows were still passed to the triage script untouched (the script gated most of them DQ/P3).
Grata variant 2 (UPS battery replacement service / data center commissioning, 32 results) was mostly on-thesis; both pages fetched (all 32 rows). 3 Grata search calls total, within the 5-call cap.

All 257 raw rows (200 Inven + 57 Grata) went to triage_xref.py unfiltered; it dropped 84 already-known and kept 173 survivors (52 DQ-candidate, 93 P2-candidate, 28 P3-candidate; 125 Inven / 48 Grata). Triage script gate/age/ownership flags are preserved verbatim in each row's note.

Notable data quirks in survivors: Northeast Generator shows founded 1694 (obvious data error, row is DQ-gated anyway); K2 Power Solutions shows founded 2024; two Grata rows are 'Investor Backed' (LIVIO, JDC Power) and carry the script's REVIEW ownership flag.

No failed or retried tool calls; both sources returned successfully. Raw and triaged files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Master-Target-List/cdc2f6cb-7804-5be0-bfc8-f894363d3735/scratchpad/xref_T6_raw.json and xref_T6_triaged.json.

Kept P2: jmschaefer.com - 'businesses and consumers' is a consumer mention but not the literal residential gate language; maintenance programs present.
Kept P2: facilityitgroup.com - IT/cloud consulting mix dilutes the electrical thesis; verify service mix.
Kept P2: aecinc.us - data inconsistency: description claims ~180 electricians vs 34 employees / $33M estimate; if 180 techs is right, revenue likely exceeds the $50M box.
Kept P2: sandhillsutility.com - single-customer (defense/Fort Bragg) concentration and 51 emp vs $5.2M rev inconsistency; both cut against the estimate.
Kept P2: electrexindustrial.com - 'process piping' is a mechanical adjacency; did not gate (not literally plumbing/HVAC) but verify.

Kept P2 with solar-share caveat: currentelectricalservices.com, sigalutility.com, eesystemsusa.com mention 'renewable energy' without a solar lead; verify solar is not the growth engine (client excludes solar).
Kept P2: jdcpowersystems.com - existing REVIEW on 'Investor Backed' ownership stands; P2 is conditional on confirming no PE sponsor. Same check applies generally to Grata 'Investor Backed' rows.
Kept P2: doyleelectricinc.com - construction-led description but explicit in-house service department; consistent with treatment of other contractor rows (Angiel, Summit).

RAMTEK, LDP, Power & Systems Innovations kept P2 consistently with the Facility Gateway/DVL un-gate rationale: mission-critical 'cooling' alongside a power-services lead is in-trade; standalone HVAC identity (access-inc.com, stillwell-hansen.com, rackelectric.com) stays gated.
DQ stands, gate-label nit: pccsinc.net was tagged 'manufacturer (self)' but is a manufacturer's REP - the distribution/resale gate is the valid one; no priority change.

DQ stands with extra reason: dekafahrenheit.com is a brand/division of East Penn Manufacturing (large parent) - subsidiary exclusion applies on top of manufacturer gate; the $10M rev row is a fragment of the parent.
Data error noted: northeastgenerator.com founding year listed as 1694; DQ (residential) unaffected.
Left P3 (marine vertical, sub-$5M): startechmarine.com, mnidiesel.com, maritimetechnicalservices.com - genuine generator/electrical service work but marine-focused and below the revenue box.

Left P3 (below box or consulting): relres.com, teamsilverback.com, feace.com, karbonengineering.com, theantaragroup.com, genelco-inc.com, gensolutionsllc.com, silverback/datacenter rows. genelco-inc.com and gensolutionsllc.com are the best trade fits here - Nurture-worthy if revenue proves above $5M.

No moves recorded: bucket definitions for T1-T5/S7-S10 were not provided, so none could be assigned with confidence. zerodbcomm.com and atni.us (fiber/telecom infrastructure services) are the clearest candidates for relocation if a telecom bucket exists.

Estimate unchanged at 13,564; ownership filter = private_unknown/family_owned/venture_capital/angel/family_office.

Inven total_results (13,564) is far broader than the S7 bucket - the semantic prompt pulled in adjacent rotating-equipment service categories. Only the top-200 relevance page was exported. Visible drift in exported rows: wind turbine O&M, aviation turbine/propeller MRO, elevator service, marine/ship repair, pump/valve/machine shops, and a few mis-geotagged non-US companies (merelectrical.co.uk = UK, qam.co.nz = NZ) that passed the US filter.

Grata variant 1 ('dynamic balancing service / vibration analysis rotating equipment'): 33 total; page 1 (25 rows) was roughly half off-thesis (general machine shops, propeller/auto/engine shops), so page 2 (8 remaining rows) was not fetched under the budget rule. Variant 2 ('generator rewind / traction motor repair'): 24 total, single page, fully retrieved. 2 Grata calls total. Grata also returned mis-geotagged non-US rows (directionswa.com.au = Australia, alpha-converting.co.uk = UK) despite locations=United States.

S7 uses a $2M-$50M revenue box (vs $5M for other buckets); the triage script's notes still reference the $5-50M box, so several $2-5M-revenue rows are labeled P3 'below $5M box' even though they are inside the S7 spec's range - worth remembering when re-ranking.

Triage script (sole dedupe/triage authority): 249 rows in (200 Inven + 49 Grata), 62 dropped as already known, 0 dropped for missing domain, 187 survivors = 110 P2-candidate, 54 P3-candidate, 23 DQ-candidate (gates: manufacturer-self, residential, off-trade HVAC/plumbing, distribution/resale). Cross-source duplicates (e.g. Lloyd Electric, Beaudry, Balance Vibration Technologies, AGTServices) were handled by the script; both an Inven and a Grata row survive for a few names where the script kept them.
No failed or retried tool calls; both sources completed normally.

Residential DQs left standing per the literal gate: emopb.com (also below $5M), emserviceinc.com, epselectric.com, morganelevator.com, coastalservice.com, doneritepumps.com.

Fair DQs left standing: advrotors.com, raven-engineering.com, columbiarubbermills.com, lyonsind.com, alpha-converting.co.uk, aem.us (manufacturer-led); aps-centraltx.com, tdirefrigeration.com, allenmitchell.com (HVAC is the delivered trade); ekstromcarlson.com (real cutting-tool manufacturing plus motor supply lines, not incidental parts sales).

notes: Inven: total_results 12594 (retrievable 10000); pulled 200 rows in the single allowed run; credits_used {screening:1, export:200, total:201}. The estimate count suggests the semantic prompt matched a very broad transportation/infrastructure universe - many returned rows are traffic engineering/design consultancies, traffic control (flagging/striping/guardrail) firms, and general civil contractors rather than signal/lighting/ITS electrical contractors; the triage script kept these as P2/P3/DQ-candidates so downstream review should weight the note field.

Inven build interpretation_notes: (a) US private-company revenue filter uses estimated latest-year revenue only (reported financials unavailable); (b) subsidiary exclusion mapped to corporate_subsidiary label, imperfect data possible; (c) clarification_needed on 'not PE-backed' - resolved from thesis as 'exclude all companies with any private equity backing' (the reading the built filters already commit to: ownershipTypes private_unknown/family_owned/venture_capital/angel/family_office). No missing_criterion entry, so no refinement pass was needed.

Grata variant 1 (ITS installation / highway lighting contractor): 11 total, all returned on page 1, mostly on-thesis. Grata variant 2 (airfield lighting maintenance / sports lighting installation): 44 total across 2 pages; page 1 (25 rows) showed heavy drift toward sports-lighting installers, sports-turf builders, generic commercial electricians, one solar firm and one fixture manufacturer, so page 2 was NOT fetched per the mostly-on-thesis rule. 2 Grata calls total (cap 5).

Triage: in=236 (200 Inven + 36 Grata), survivors=189, dropped_known=47, nodomain=0. Cross-source overlap visible: Paradigm Traffic Systems appears from both Inven and Grata variant 1 with different revenue estimates (both survived triage as written). All rows were passed to the triage script unfiltered; no rows were dropped by me (dropped_offthesis=0).
No failed calls; both sources completed on first attempt.
verify_notes: Off-thesis policy applied: ~57 rows are pure engineering/planning/design/CEI/CM consultancies (professional services firms with licensed-engineer economics, no self-performed electrical or field service work). They are not electrical infrastructure services businesses and were false positives from the S8 keyword search; all moved to offthesis rather than corrected. If the client runs a separate transportation-engineering-services thesis, this list is a ready-made seed for it.

Off-thesis policy applied: pure heavy-civil/paving/excavation contractors (larryyoungpaving, lead-ec, jvaengineering, lesnainc, denucciconstructors, alliedcontractor, coulsonex), sports-turf builders (appliedlt, t3globalprojects), telecom infrastructure (ngtgroupllc, sncsolution), federal ops-support/air-traffic-control (kayacorp), and transit-amenity products (futuresystems-inc) have no electrical services line at all.

Non-electrical roadway-safety FIELD SERVICE firms (flagging, striping, guardrail, MOT, attenuators) were downgraded to P3 with REVIEW-bucket flags rather than DQ'd or moved: they are genuinely service/maintenance-led and may fit a sibling roadway-services bucket, but the S8 thesis says electrical. No moves recorded because T1-T6/S7/S9/S10 definitions were not provided to this verifier.

Verified and kept at P2 (all four legs pass on the given data): reedwick.com, jhe-la.com, deco-la.com, fie-inc.com, acstraffic.net, sawyer-services.com, integral-blue.com, olympicelectric.net, glenelgconstruction.com, alleghenycityelectric.com, southerncontracting.com, coloradolighting.com, tankolighting.com, rjhaynie.com, groveselectric.com, efbelkelectric.com, systemselectricalservices.com, ncobbelectrical.com, danielselectric.com.

Residential DQs upheld per the client's literal gate even where the business is otherwise attractive: cmhigh.com in particular has explicit 'traffic signal maintenance' and would be a strong P2 if the gate is ever relaxed - flag to client. bagrus.com, agcelectric.com, mbelectric.com, hirschelectricllc.com, allowayelectric.com, usacontinental.com, extremeelectricalstl.com also stand.

Other DQs upheld as fair in context: trafficcontrolcorp.com, its-products.com, nextechsystemsinc.com ('operates as a distributor'), cpcsigns.com, tssco.com, addco.com, amsig.com, rtc-traffic.com, ssasenterprises.com, nationalssc.com, elteccorp.com, qualite.com, minichiinc.com (solar farm construction is a real line), nlmsinc.com, knightelectric.net (HVAC co-equal in description), westelectrical.com (fire alarm line plus retail supply outlet), thebartechgroup.biz (security systems is an actual listed service line, unlike schupps.com where it was incidental).

Data-integrity anomalies for the enrichment pass: reedwick.com founded 2019 but claims '30+ years experience'; glenelgconstruction.com $28.5M on 10 employees and kantaelectric.com $29.3M on 14 employees are implausible revenue/headcount ratios; lighthousetg.org $48.6M / 25 emp / founded 2022; raderexcavating.com HQ Tennessee vs description California; coulsonex.com HQ New York vs description Northern Colorado; addco.com HQ 'Saint Paul, Alaska' looks like a bad merge; esgcorp domain is a sitebuilder subdomain, not a real corporate domain.

Possible related entities: jhe-la.com (Jack B. Harper Electrical, Walker LA) and jbhcontractor.com (Jack B Harper Contractor, Covington LA) share a name and state - verify common ownership before counting them as two targets.

notes: Inven build flagged a missing_criterion ('not venture backed' not expressed as a filter) and a clarification_needed on 'not PE-backed'. Resolved per thesis: VC-backed private companies stay in (the spec's VC phrase is a business-model exclusion of asset-owning charging networks, carried in the semantic prompt), PE-backed/public/subsidiaries excluded via ownershipTypes. The one refinement attempt dropped the descriptivePrompt entirely (unranked ~373K results, flagged broken by interpretation_notes), so the ORIGINAL search_id (3dd8a751, ~24,178 est. results, semantic prompt intact) was run instead - its filters already matched the resolution. Exactly one run call was made.
Inven total_results 24,178 (retrievable 10,000); only the top-200 semantically ranked rows were exported (200 export + 1 screening credits). Tail beyond 200 unexamined.

Grata variant 1 (EV charger maintenance / DC fast charger installation): 83 total, page 1 (25 rows) drifted heavily into residential/solar/generalist electricians that merely mention EV chargers, so page 2 was NOT fetched. Variant 2 (fleet electrification infrastructure services): 1 total result (Skycharger, a build-own-operate network - likely off-thesis, but left to triage). 2 Grata calls total = 6 tokens.

Triage: 226 raw rows in, 175 survivors, 51 dropped as already-known, 0 dropped for missing domain. Survivor priorities: 52 P2-candidate, 26 P3-candidate, 97 DQ-candidate (mostly residential/solar/home-services/off-trade gates). Sources of survivors: 157 Inven, 18 Grata.

Material drift in Inven results too: many survivors are generalist electrical contractors, telecom/tower, signage, or parking-management companies that mention EV charging, and several are VC-funded network owner/operators (Terawatt, Ionna, EVCS, Xeal, Chargie, Francis Energy) that the spec excludes by business model - the script's REVIEW notes flag ownership, but network-owner status needs human screen. Strong-looking on-thesis names include ChargerHelp, Speed Charge Services (getspeedcharge.com), OhmNow, Smart Charge America, Verdek, ZEF Energy, Heartland Charging Services, National Car Charging.

Data quality: 'Alpha Elektro AS' (alphaelektro.no) is a Norwegian Oslo-area company mislocated by Inven as Hagan, Georgia US; 'Fargo Assembly Company' (fargopa.com) row carries a description for 'Prairie Electric' - both left in per triage-authority rule.
dropped_offthesis is 0 by instruction: no rows were filtered or dropped outside the triage script.
verify_notes: P2 survivors after adversarial pass (unchanged): verdek.com, pevarnik.com, bluewhaleev.com, goforthelectric.com, henderson-services.com, bescoelectrical.com, crawford-electric.com, landmarkelectricinc.com, centralstateco.com, mojaveelectric.com, kentelectricinc.com, aetnacorp.com, coloradolighting.com, psserv.com, retrofitcompanies.com, neoelectrical.com - these show C&I electrical service/maintenance delivery, in-box revenue, no exclusion language, and no sponsor recorded.

Ownership policy applied: rows with own=venture_capital or 'Investor Backed' were treated as sponsored. Thesis-perfect service businesses (chargerhelp.com, energysource.com, green-wealth.com) went to Nurture-candidate pending ownership confirmation; VC rows that also failed the service-led leg went to DQ.

Telecom-infrastructure rows (ampcommunications.com, metrorf.com, attowers.com, txnwireless.com, techconstruction.org, utiligi.com) were downgraded to P3 for trade fit. They may belong in a telecom-services bucket, but T1-T6/S7-S10 definitions were not provided, so no moves were recorded - flag for the orchestrator.

Residential gate extended literally and consistently: smartchargeamerica.com ('home and commercial... individual consumers') and smartpowersi.com ('for homes and businesses') were DQ'd on the same standard the deterministic gate applied elsewhere. All existing residential DQs were checked and left in place per instructions, including multifamily phrasings (refuelevs.com, buzze.biz, evmatch.com, energyone.biz).

Gate corrections: facilico.com and divienergy.com were gated solely on 'HVAC control wiring'/'HVAC controls' - controls wiring is electrical scope, not the mechanical HVAC trade; both restored with REVIEW notes. evnoire.com's 'vehicle dealership' gate is technically misapplied (they certify dealerships, they are not one), but the firm is a consulting company and off-thesis regardless - DQ stands.

Data-integrity flags: fargopa.com's description is for a different company ('Prairie Electric'); Fargo Assembly is a wire-harness manufacturer - DQ stands but the record needs re-enrichment. alphaelektro.no is a Norwegian company (Oslo/Akershus; the Georgia HQ is a geocoding error) - outside the US thesis; existing DQ stands. getspeedcharge.com carries the FreeWire Technologies name with 220 employees against $3.7M revenue - likely describes FreeWire's service arm; subsidiary risk if it ever moves up from P3.

Revenue-credibility flags on retained/downgraded rows: amfacpro.com ($16.8M/10 emp), ev.pro ($17.9M/10 emp), neoelectrical.com ($16M/12 emp), techconstruction.org ($12.4M/12 emp). Estimates sit in the box but revenue-per-head is implausible for services firms; verify before outreach.

EV charging network owner-operators (CPOs) were distinguished from service providers: owning and operating charging assets (terawatt, evcs, ionna, francisenergy, chargie) is not service/maintenance delivery to third parties, which is what the S9 thesis buys.

chenaultconsulting.com left P3 with rev ~$141M (far above box) and an oil/gas PM/inspection profile at the edge of the trade; industrialaccess.com left P3 above box as noted.

No moves recorded: candidate off-trade rows (gas piping, diving, civil GC, marine, safety) were gated as off-trade DQs because the definitions of buckets T1-T6/S7-S9 were not provided, so a confident re-bucketing was not possible from the data given.

Off-thesis pulls are pure equipment OEMs with no service line in their descriptions (prosurge.com, empshield.com, maxivolt.com, galvotec.com, borin.com), an industrial gasket/fastener maker-distributor (ccgasket.com), a tree-care firm (arborct.com), and an environmental consultancy (commonwealthenvironmental.com). gaps: Inven depth untested in every bucket: only the top-200 relevance-ranked rows of universes between 3,077 (S10) and 24,414 (T4) were exported, and observed drift shows generic contractors/distributors occupying much of page 1 - meaning true on-thesis firms were outranked and sit in the unexamined tail. No offset paging was exercised anywhere (T6's own note recommends it). This is the single largest recall gap across all 10 buckets.

Accreditation-directory modality never exercised despite four buckets being accreditation-defined: NETA member directory (T1), EASA/PEARL member lists (T2, S7), LPI/UL Master Label listings (S10). These are small, enumerable, authoritative universes; semantic search demonstrably failed on exactly these buckets (T1: 13,266-result estimate for a few-hundred-firm NETA universe, 160/269 rows already known, drift dominating the rest; S10: nearly all true lightning-protection installers surfaced were already known). Wave 3 should scrape directories, not re-run embeddings.

Grata budget systematically under-used: 2-3 calls of the 5-call cap per bucket, and page 2 skipped whenever page 1 looked mixed - but page-1 mix is a ranking artifact, not proof the residue is bad. Concretely unexamined: T1 variant 1 (154 of 179 rows unseen), T5 both variants (233 and 137 unseen), T6 variant 1 (206 unseen), S9 variant 1 (58 unseen), S10 variant 1 page 2. No Grata find_similar_companies lookalike expansion off confirmed-good wave-1/wave-2 targets was run at all in wave 2, though the repo's add_similar.py shows the modality exists.

T5 is the worst under-return relative to market: 19 net-new P2 against a Grata-measured universe of ~1,256 commercial electrical service firms (842 in the $5-50M box). The Inven prompt drifted to MRO/distributor language and the two Grata variants were sampled at 25 rows each. T5 needs a re-run with contractor-service-department-specific phrasing, not more of the same.

T6 and T4 similarly thin vs. market size: T6 delivered 47 net-new P2 against a ~3,018-firm universe (1,264 in box); T4 delivered 63 against ~1,718 (1,131 in box). Both buckets' Inven pages were mostly usable, so paging deeper (offset 200-600) is cheap incremental coverage.

Both platforms share a systematic surface bias the sweep never compensated for: description-embedding search rewards firms with rich web copy, and install/construction/product language outranks service language. The actual target profile - small, old, family-owned service shops with weak websites (cf. moodyselectricinc.godaddysites.com) - is exactly what this modality under-surfaces. No offline modality (state contractor-license registries, trade-association rosters, conference exhibitor lists like PowerTest/EASA convention) was used to reach them.

T4 Grata results structurally exclude pre-1965 companies: year_founded_max=2016 was translated to company_age [10,61], silently cutting firms founded before ~1965 - i.e., the oldest family-owned businesses, prime targets for this thesis. No other bucket checked whether its Grata age translation has the same floor.

Ownership filtering is inconsistent across buckets for the same thesis phrase 'not PE-backed': T1's refinement silently dropped venture_capital (VC-backed privates excluded); T2/T5/S7/S8 included VC/angel; S9 deliberately included VC; S10 excluded both PE and VC. T1 (and S10) may have silently excluded legitimate targets; the buckets' P2 pools are not comparable on ownership. The clarification was never put to the client in any bucket.

Verifiers were not given the T1-T6/S7-S10 bucket definitions, so cross-bucket re-homing was impossible by design - 'no moves recorded' appears in 8+ verifier notes. Combined with order-based cross-bucket dedupe (see anomalies), mis-homed rows are now stranded: motor/rewind shops sit in T4/T5 instead of S7 (brandonclark, electricmotorshop, vaughnelectric, texasoilelectric, aandwelectric and the T5 motor cluster), telecom/fiber rows recur in T3/T6/S9 with no bucket to receive them, S8's roadway-safety field-service firms are parked at P3, and aviation-MRO rows went to Nurture/offthesis. A re-homing pass with definitions in hand is missing.

No geography-verification step exists: at least 14 confirmed non-US companies passed the US HQ filter across 7+ buckets (merelectrical.co.uk, sandtsystems.co.uk, behncke.de, neo-cam.org in two buckets, Navitas .rs, melconltd.co.uk, metrowest.com.au, dahlrail.com, access-electrical.co.uk, alphaelektro.no, qam.co.nz, directionswa.com.au, alpha-converting.co.uk, stonetechnicalgroup.co.uk). TLD/description-vs-HQ checks are trivial to automate and were not run.

The ~556 DQ-candidates across the wave are a known-contaminated pool with no recovery process: verifiers found gate misfires in nearly every bucket they checked (auigroup.com T3; primeelectrical.net, graphicelectric.org, smartelectriccompanyinc.com T4; facilico.com, divienergy.com S9; dreisilker.com T5; theprotectionsource.com S10 flagged as likely misread), plus strong firms killed by the literal any-mention residential gate (cmhigh.com with explicit traffic-signal maintenance, blackwaterelectric.com, beckstromelectric.com, hannonelectricinc.com). The client has never been asked whether the residential/fire-alarm/solar gates are any-mention or lead-line; that one question changes dozens of verdicts.

S7's $2-50M revenue box was never propagated into the triage script, which applied the $5M floor - so S7 P3 counts include in-spec $2-5M firms mislabeled 'below box' (sidewindersllc.com and sheppardsvs.com sit at the boundary). Wind-turbine O&M rows (6 kept in S7) and cathodic-protection rows (dominant among new S10 finds) both await a client in/out-of-thesis ruling that no one has requested.

S9 coverage of the actual thesis (third-party EV-charger service/maintenance) is near-zero after filtering: 14 P2 from 157 new, and the strongest names the sweep note itself lists (ChargerHelp, Speed Charge, etc.) mostly landed in Nurture/P3 on ownership or subsidiary doubts. The bucket needs a targeted modality (EVSE O&M certification lists, ChargePoint/EVgo service-partner networks) rather than keyword search that returns residential electricians who mention chargers.

Nurture is effectively unused as a category: 12 Nurture-candidates across 1,365 new rows, 8 of them T2 aviation/marine misfits used as a dumping ground. In-thesis-but-out-of-box names explicitly called 'Nurture-worthy' by verifiers (genelco-inc.com, gensolutionsllc.com in T6) were left at P3; no tracking path exists for them.
anomalies: The tally's 'new' counts do not equal survivors minus offthesis in 9 of 10 buckets - 186 rows vanish (T2:6, T3:2, T4:31, T5:38, T6:18, S7:52, S8:9, S9:9, S10:21). I reproduced this computationally from the triaged files: it is order-based cross-bucket dedupe in sequence T1->S10 (first bucket to surface a domain keeps it; my recount matches the deltas exactly except S7, 53 vs 52 - even the dedupe accounting is off by one). Nothing in the tally or notes discloses this. The keep-assignment is processing order, not thesis fit: S7 lost 52 rows - largely motor-shop names that are S7's core - to drift buckets T2/T4/T5 that happened to surface them first. Concrete casualty: westelectrical.com is DQ-candidate in S8 but P2-candidate in S10; which verdict survived depends solely on bucket order.

150 domains appear in more than one bucket's survivor list (32 in three or more, e.g. aandwelectric.com, electricmotorshop.com, scottarm.com, vaughnelectric.com, rileyelectricco.com). Verifiers then re-diligenced the same company under different buckets with no reconciliation - aecinc.us carries the identical unresolved 180-electricians-vs-34-employees contradiction in both T4 and T6 notes; glenelgconstruction.com is a 'clean P2 confirm' in T3 while S8 flags its $28.5M-on-10-employees ratio as implausible; eliteelectrical.net's 83-emp/$7.6M conflict is independently flagged in T2 and T4.

T5 cannot be reconciled with its own verifier: the verifier lists ~47 named P2s that 'survived challenge' but the tally records P2=19. Cross-bucket dedupe presumably removed ~28, but no record states which of the 47 remain - the T5 P2 list as written is unusable for outreach until regenerated.

'dropped_known' conflates within-wave cross-source dupes with genuinely already-known companies: T4's note counts B.L. Smith among its 81 'known' drops, yet blsmithelectric.com is a T4 P2 survivor (the Grata copy was dropped, the Inven copy kept) and it is absent from the master dedupe index. The 739 total dropped_known therefore overstates prior-list overlap by an unquantified amount, and the wave's 'coverage saturation' cannot be inferred from it.

Sweep notes contain false claims about their own outputs: S8's note says Paradigm Traffic Systems 'appears from both Inven and Grata... both survived triage' - the triaged file contains exactly one Paradigm row; S7's note says 'both an Inven and a Grata row survive for a few names' - S7 survivors contain zero duplicate names or domains. The notes are unreliable as an audit trail; anything load-bearing should be re-derived from the files.

Same-company revenue estimates differ across sources by up to 4.9x and cross the $5-50M box boundary, invalidating box-based priority calls: emoryelectric.com $40.9M vs $51.3M (in-box vs out), tomcoelectric.com $18.2M vs $47.9M, krautomationinc.com $5.5M vs $27.1M, aem.us $9.7M vs $44.6M. Every P3 'below box' and every box-pass rests on estimates this noisy; the workbook cuts.json meta confirms reported financials are unavailable for US privates.

S9 Nurture arithmetic: the verifier names three Nurture moves (chargerhelp.com, energysource.com, green-wealth.com) but the tally records Nurture-candidate=2 - one row lost or miscounted. T1 shows Nurture-candidate=1 with no verifier note explaining any Nurture move at all.

T3's numbers are internally impossible as bucket coverage: 137 'new' with 113 P2+P3 against a Grata-measured T3 universe of ~102 companies total (68 in box), 58 of the raw rows already known. New finds exceeding the measurable market means most T3 'new' rows are drift (telecom/pipeline/civil) - the 30 P2 / 83 P3 split should not be presented to the client as T3 pipeline without a manual on-thesis pass, which the sweep note itself requests.

T2's 78 new P2s against a ~273-firm universe (142 in box, 70 raw rows already known) implies wave 2 alone found over half the remaining market - not credible. The number is inflated by (a) the refinement that loosened the search 10x (estimate 1,852 -> 19,739, the opposite of its purpose) and (b) the verifier's explicit unconfirmed assumption keeping the ~10-name servo/PLC/industrial-electronics repair cluster at P2; if the client reads the thesis as power infrastructure only, T2 P2 drops by roughly a third. Two rows the sweep passed as P2 (signalfluidsolutions.com, bjsoilfield.com, alaresengineering.com) had no electrical service at all.

The triage script's P2 gate is systematically broken: the boilerplate note 'service/maintenance/testing language' was attached to rows whose descriptions contain no such language, found independently by three verifiers (T3: 79 downgrades, T4: ~30, T5: 25+ distributors mislabeled P2). S8 is the extreme case - triage marked 144 of 189 survivors P2, final count 17 (88% of the P2 signal wrong). Any P2 count from this wave that did not receive a full adversarial verify should be treated as inflated.

Row-level data errors that survived into deliverable files and should be spot-checked before the client sees them: Northeast Generator founded '1694'; fargopa.com carrying Prairie Electric's description; alphaelektro.no geocoded to Hagan, Georgia; addco.com HQ 'Saint Paul, Alaska'; melconltd.co.uk labeled Hereford TX; reedwick.com founded 2019 claiming '30+ years'; lighthousetg.org $48.6M / 25 emp / founded 2022; kantaelectric.com $29.3M on 14 employees; linearelec.com $35.6M/22 emp, espohio.com $30.5M/18 emp, powersubservices.com $15.3M/11 emp, amfacpro.com and ev.pro ~$17M on 10 employees each - plus the inverse cases (electricianoncall.com 166 emp/$8.4M).

T1's refinement silently narrowed ownership (venture_capital dropped from included types) with no client sign-off - materially different from every other bucket's filter and unflagged in the tally. Combined with the T2 refinement loosening 10x, both buckets' refinement passes changed scope in ways their estimates reveal but their notes underplay.
